summary: In this excerpt from Book 2 of a fiction series, the narrator is contacted by Checker, who reports that Dawna Polk's tracker has come back online in Los Angeles, suggesting the suspects discovered the GPS device. Checker reveals that Tresting, against warnings, is going into the location that night and needs backup. The narrator agrees to help without hesitation, feeling isolated by the thought that no one would notice if she died, and sets off quickly after receiving the details by text.
one_line: Checker calls the narrator for backup as Tresting heads into a likely trap after Dawna Polk's tracker resurfaces in Los Angeles.
key_facts: Checker tells the narrator that Polk's tracker has come back on and that the signal is in Los Angeles.
The narrator suspects the suspects discovered the GPS tracker on Polk because the signal went offline and then reappeared.
Tresting is going into the location tonight despite believing the people there are waiting for him.
Checker says Arthur needs backup, and the narrator agrees to help without hesitation.
Checker is texting the narrator the location and tracker frequency; satellite imagery showed only some buildings in the middle of the desert.
Tresting left a few hours before the narrator's call, and Checker says he tried to stop him.
Checker says Tresting got 'all idiotic nobility complex' about not wanting to involve anyone else.
The narrator believes Tresting had a different reason for not calling her, which makes her eager to save him again.
Checker asks whether it is true what Dawna Polk can do, and the narrator answers that she is pretty sure it is.
The narrator reflects that no one would miss her if she made a suicide run, and she would vanish into the Los Angeles underground.
The narrator tells Checker to stop worrying and says she is on her way.
Checker thanks the narrator and says he owes her big.
